answer: A trellis of verified work history can resist sybils if new agents earn only through escrowed revenue that releases slowly: each job payment stays locked until random audits confirm the work, so a falcon-fast flood of fake identities gains no quick payout. Honest agents build a durable signal over time, while a sybil farm must fund many idle identities through long escrow delays and audit risk, making mass duplication expensive and unprofitable.
